title: Tenable Windows Vulnerability Assessment
summary: Windows endpoint vulnerability assessment using Tenable Vulnerability Management—scanning systems, analyzing findings, prioritizing remediation, and documenting the workflow with sensitive details redacted.
objective: Identify security weaknesses on Windows endpoints, analyze risk with CVSS and vendor guidance, prioritize remediation, and validate fixes through follow-up review.
workedOn: Organized managed Windows endpoints for assessment using generalized tagging practices
Ran authenticated vulnerability scans and reviewed discovered findings
Researched associated CVEs and vendor advisories
Prioritized vulnerabilities by severity, exploitability, and practical impact
Recommended remediation actions and verified mitigation through follow-up assessment
Published sanitized documentation with hostnames, IPs, and internal details removed

details.overview: A documented vulnerability-management project focused on assessing Windows systems with Tenable Vulnerability Management. The work covers scanning, finding analysis, remediation planning, and validation—presented without exposing real organizational infrastructure.
details.businessProblem: Windows endpoints accumulate missing patches and configuration weaknesses over time. Without structured scanning and prioritization, high-risk issues can linger while lower-risk noise consumes attention.
details.environment: Managed Windows endpoints assessed through Tenable Vulnerability Management. Specific hostnames, IP addresses, scan configurations, asset identifiers, and account details are intentionally redacted in the public repository.
responsibilities: Identify and organize Windows assets for assessment
Execute and review authenticated vulnerability scans
Analyze findings using CVSS scores and vendor advisories
Recommend practical remediation and confirm mitigation
process: Identified managed Windows endpoints for assessment
Organized assets using generalized tagging practices
Ran vulnerability scans using an authenticated assessment approach
Reviewed and validated discovered findings
Researched associated CVEs and vendor guidance
Prioritized vulnerabilities based on risk
Recommended remediation actions
Verified mitigation through follow-up review
details.results: Built a clear, recruiter-friendly record of vulnerability management practice—including sample analyses (for example, Microsoft Edge and WinVerifyTrust findings)—while keeping all sensitive operational data out of the public write-up.

title: Infoblox NIOS Enterprise DDI Lab
summary: Hands-on lab documenting enterprise DNS, DHCP, and IPAM administration with Infoblox NIOS 9.0—covering Grid architecture, service validation, troubleshooting, and technical documentation.
objective: Understand how enterprise organizations centrally manage DNS, DHCP, and IP address allocation, and produce clear documentation of discovery, validation, and troubleshooting work.
workedOn: Explored and documented a simulated Infoblox Grid across multiple network locations
Studied Grid architecture spanning primary/secondary datacenters and a branch office
Validated DNS resolution, DHCP assignment, and IPAM utilization
Tested client connectivity on Windows and Linux systems
Documented troubleshooting methodology and lessons learned

details.overview: A structured lab that explores administration, validation, and troubleshooting of a simulated enterprise DDI environment using Infoblox NIOS 9.0. Documentation covers environment discovery through lessons learned.
details.businessProblem: Growing organizations need centralized DNS, DHCP, and IP address management across multiple sites. Without clear Grid understanding and validation practices, network services become harder to operate and troubleshoot.
details.environment: Simulated enterprise network with multiple Infoblox Grid appliances, primary and secondary datacenters, a branch office, routing infrastructure, reporting services, and Windows/Linux clients.
responsibilities: Explore the existing Infoblox Grid and document infrastructure
Understand Grid architecture and IP address information
Validate DNS and DHCP services and client connectivity
Troubleshoot network service issues and produce technical documentation
process: Repository and documentation setup
Environment discovery
Grid architecture review
IPAM, DNS, and DHCP administration
Client validation and troubleshooting
Lessons learned and final documentation
details.results: Produced a recruiter-friendly documentation set covering DDI concepts, Grid architecture, validation steps, and troubleshooting methodology for an enterprise Infoblox NIOS environment.

title: QueryShield
summary: Full-stack service that analyzes SQL query strings for injection indicators, assigns risk scores and severity levels, and surfaces results through authenticated API endpoints and a React dashboard.
objective: Provide a pre-execution inspection layer that reviews SQL queries for suspicious constructs, scores risk, and stores analysis history for authenticated users.
workedOn: Built a FastAPI backend with JWT authentication and protected analysis endpoints
Implemented pattern detection for injection indicators such as always-true conditions, comment truncation, and UNION-based attacks
Assigned weighted risk scores and severity classifications (low through critical)
Persisted analysis results in PostgreSQL tied to authenticated users
Created a React dashboard for live analysis, history, and high-risk filtering
Containerized the stack with Docker Compose and deployed to AWS EC2

details.overview: QueryShield is a SQL injection risk analysis API with a React web UI. It inspects query strings before execution, detects suspicious patterns, calculates a risk score, and returns a structured security report.
details.businessProblem: SQL injection remains a common web application risk. Teams need a practical way to inspect query strings, score risk, and review historical high-risk examples without waiting for production exploitation.
details.environment: Python/FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy, JWT auth, React + TypeScript frontend, Docker Compose locally, and deployment on AWS EC2.
responsibilities: Design and implement the risk analysis engine and API routes
Build dashboard flows for analysis, history, and high-risk views
Package and deploy the service with Docker on AWS EC2
process: Receive an authenticated analysis request
Run pattern detection against the query string
Calculate risk score and severity classification
Store the result in PostgreSQL
Return a structured JSON report to the client or dashboard
details.results: Delivered an end-to-end defensive security service demonstrating backend API design, secure authentication, database persistence, containerization, and cloud deployment applied to SQL injection risk analysis.

title: ReadScope
summary: Backend-driven reading analytics platform that compares an expected passage to a spoken transcript, then returns accuracy, fluency heuristics, and detailed error feedback with authenticated session history.
objective: Evaluate reading performance by tokenizing expected and spoken text, identifying matches and mismatches, and returning scored analysis tied to user accounts.
workedOn: Built FastAPI routes for authentication, reading sessions, and analysis
Implemented JWT auth with bcrypt password hashing and user-scoped data access
Created an analysis service that normalizes text, counts word frequencies, and scores accuracy/fluency
Modeled users, sessions, and analysis results with PostgreSQL and SQLAlchemy
Scaffolded a React + Vite frontend for future UI work

details.overview: ReadScope compares what a user was supposed to read with what they actually said. It returns scored analysis and feedback, with full session history for authenticated users.
details.businessProblem: Reading practice needs measurable feedback. Comparing expected text to a transcript gives concrete accuracy and fluency signals instead of informal review alone.
details.environment: Python 3.10+, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, JWT authentication, Pydantic validation, Uvicorn. React + Vite frontend is scaffolded.
responsibilities: Implement auth, session, and analysis API endpoints
Build the text comparison and scoring service
Keep session and analysis data scoped to the authenticated user
process: Create an authenticated reading session with source and transcript text
Normalize and tokenize both texts
Identify matched, missing, and extra words
Calculate accuracy and fluency scores and store the analysis result
details.results: Shipped a working backend analysis pipeline with authenticated session history. Comprehension scoring and audio transcription remain on the project roadmap.

title: Courtside Coach AI
summary: Hackathon project that sends a basketball court diagram and play-by-play transcript to a multimodal Llama 4 model to identify momentum-shifting plays, with a Flask API and React frontend.
objective: Ingest a court diagram image and play-by-play text, then use Llama 4 Scout to locate and explain the most momentum-shifting three-pointer in the selected quarter or full game.
workedOn: Wrote a Python analysis script that encodes a court diagram and pairs it with play-by-play text for Llama 4 Scout
Built a Flask API endpoint that accepts court image data, transcript text, and quarter selection
Filtered transcripts by quarter before sending them to the model
Created a React frontend for interacting with the analysis API

details.overview: Courtside Coach AI is a multimodal Llama 4 hackathon project. It combines a court diagram with basketball play-by-play text and asks the model to identify where the most momentum-shifting three-pointer occurred and why it mattered.
details.businessProblem: Game film and play-by-play logs are dense. A prototype multimodal workflow can highlight key momentum moments faster than manual review alone.
details.environment: Python analysis scripts and Flask backend calling an OpenAI-compatible Llama API; React frontend deployed via GitHub Pages.
responsibilities: Prepare multimodal inputs (Base64 court image + transcript)
Expose an /analyze API with quarter filtering
Connect a React UI to the analysis backend
process: Load or upload a court diagram and play-by-play transcript
Optionally filter the transcript to a selected quarter
Send image and text to Llama-4-Scout through the compatibility API
Return a structured explanation of the momentum-shifting play
details.results: Produced a working multimodal prototype that demonstrates prompt design, API integration, and full-stack wiring around Llama 4. This project shows applied AI engineering interest; AI/LLM security remains a separate career focus area.
